approved_findings: New versus old raw preserves four ACH SEC codes, business responsibility for the correct code, WEB/CCD defaults when no mandate collection method is specified, WEB consumer/refund PPD behavior, CCD application to account_holder_type=company, and PPD written/signed consumer authorization and copy requirement (old lines 8-28; new lines 9-29). No captured evidence changes those semantics.

New raw lines 31-49 replace old Node PaymentIntent/SetupIntent confirmation examples (old lines 30-82) with curl. Both specify offline customer acceptance, accepted_at, and us_bank_account mandate collection_method=paper. This is an example-language change, not a new API requirement or SDK deprecation.

New raw lines 51-53 relabel TEL from old Beta/private beta (old lines 84-86) to Private preview. This is a material dated availability-label change, but does not establish access for a particular account. Source line 24, concept lines 106 and 128, and Stripe index line 248 retain beta wording and should be updated to captured private-preview wording.

Existing source line 24 says TEL requires an existing relationship, and concept line 108 repeats it. Both old raw lines 94-101 and new raw lines 61-68 permit the alternative where there is no existing relationship but the customer initiated the call. The affiliate relationship alone does not qualify. Queue a source and concept correction for this pre-existing material overstatement, separately from the small new/old delta.

Existing source line 32 says a specific oral authorization script is required. Raw line 76 requires explicit oral authorization with online-mandate information and a telephone number for inquiries; lines 78-82 present recording or pre-first-debit written notice and a sample script. The sample wording should not be elevated to a verbatim script mandate. Source line 31 and concept line 108 also need to keep written notice timing before the first debit.

TEL remains single-entry only, not standing or recurring, with commercially reasonable identity and routing-number verification (old lines 90-111; new lines 55-78). PPD offline acceptance does not substitute for TEL preview access or its separate authorization rules.
approved_conflicts: Source line 24 and concept line 108 wrongly make existing relationship universally required for TEL, contrary to both captures' customer-initiated-call alternative (old line 99; new line 66).
Source line 32 says the specific sample oral script is required, while the raw states required authorization content and gives sample wording (old lines 109-115; new lines 76-82).
Source line 24, concept lines 106/128 and Stripe index line 248 retain private-beta wording after new raw line 53 says private preview; neither phrase proves live access.
historical_claims_to_preserve: WEB is the default consumer SEC code absent a specified collection method, CCD the default business code; CCD applies to account_holder_type=company regardless of authorization type (old lines 12-22; new lines 13-23).
WEB covers internet/mobile consumer debits, while WEB refunds use PPD (old line 18; new line 19).

PPD involves standing or single-entry written/signed or otherwise authenticated consumer authorization, a copy to the customer, and offline acceptance with collection_method=paper (old lines 24-28; new lines 25-29).

TEL permits single debit entries only; eligibility includes either qualifying existing merchant-customer relationship or a customer-initiated call, with no affiliate-only substitution (old lines 84-101; new lines 51-68).
TEL requires verification, explicit oral authorization, and recording or written notice before the first debit; preview status must remain dated (old lines 103-115; new lines 70-82).
unresolved_questions: Captured documentation does not establish whether a specific Stripe account has TEL private-preview access or satisfy applicable Nacha or recording-law obligations.
The page does not establish an effective date for the beta-to-private-preview label change beyond its two capture dates.
